notes.meaning: God warns his people not to envy wicked men or desire to spend time with them. Even if evil people look successful, their hearts are busy planning harm and their words cause damage to others. Wanting to be around them pulls a person into their destructive ways.

A strong household and family are built through godly wisdom and good judgment. When people live by God's truth, their homes are filled with lasting blessings, peaceful security, and true riches. These treasures include both honest daily provisions and spiritual gifts from the Holy Spirit.

True wisdom gives a person far greater strength than mere physical power. Wise leaders do not rush into battle on their own, but succeed because they gather guidance from many trusted advisers. Victory and safety come when people humbly seek good counsel before making important moves.

Wisdom seems far too high and unreachable to a fool who refuses to put in the work to learn. Because he has no real understanding, he has nothing helpful to say when leaders meet at the city gate to handle public business. His silence in public gatherings shows how unprepared he is.

A person who deliberately plans evil against others earns the reputation of being a schemer. Even if he tries to hide his bad motives behind polite words, his habit of plotting trouble will eventually be exposed. People soon learn not to trust someone who constantly invents ways to do harm.

Devising foolish and wicked plans is itself a sin in the sight of God. Even evil thoughts that never turn into open actions displease the Lord and need forgiveness. A proud mocker who insults others and scoffs at goodness ends up being hated by everyone around him.

Giving up and losing heart when hard times strike reveals how weak a person's inner strength really is. Trouble tests a person's faith and courage like nothing else. Instead of sinking into despair, believers are called to trust God to uphold and strengthen their hearts.

God commands his people to step in and rescue innocent people who are being dragged off to die unjustly. Pretending not to know about someone else's danger will never fool God, who examines every secret thought of the human heart. The Lord who protects our own lives sees our true motives and will hold each person accountable for failing to help.

Just as sweet honey from the comb tastes delightful and nourishes the body, so God's wisdom brings deep joy and health to the soul. Those who seek and find this wisdom receive a bright future and a hope that will never be destroyed. Living by God's truth satisfies a person today and guarantees eternal rewards ahead.

The teacher warns the wicked not to lurk like robbers near the home of an innocent, righteous person. Trying to raid an upright neighbor's dwelling or steal his peace is completely futile. God watches over the resting place of those who honor him and will not let violence win.

A righteous person may face severe troubles again and again, but by God's help he recovers and gets back up every time. The wicked, however, have no such divine support and collapse completely when disaster strikes. God preserves those who trust him through many hardships, while evil finally ruins the ungodly.

differ.view: Some hold that while the verse mainly means suffering, it also shows that a truly righteous person may stumble into sin, yet God's grace preserves them from falling away completely and grants them repentance.
The verse speaks entirely of falling into outward calamities and distresses, so it should not be applied to falling into sin or used to argue for unconditional eternal security.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Preachers historically applied this passage to moral weaknesses, teaching that a righteous person might fall into venial (lesser) sins multiple times a day while still remaining in God's love.

notes.meaning: God strictly forbids taking pleasure when an enemy falls into trouble or stumbles into ruin. The Lord sees the secret gloating of the heart and is deeply displeased by such cruelty. If someone delights in another person's pain, the Lord may withhold his punishment from the offender and discipline the gloater instead.

Believers must not become angry or jealous when they see evil people thriving in this world. The wicked have no lasting future, and their shining prosperity is like a lamp that will soon be snuffed out. Looking ahead to God's final judgment frees our hearts from burning with envy over temporary success.

Children of wisdom are told to fear the Lord and show proper respect to the king God has placed over them. They must stay away from rebellious troublemakers who seek political or religious upheaval for its own sake. Disaster will fall swiftly and without warning on rebels, bringing sudden ruin upon both them and their companions.

Showing favoritism in court or in any place of judgment is completely wrong. Judges must decide cases based on truth and evidence, not on personal friendships, wealth, or social rank. Perverting justice under the guise of the law dishonors God and harms the whole community.

Any judge or leader who lets a guilty criminal off by calling him innocent will be cursed and detested by entire nations. On the other hand, leaders who faithfully convict and punish wrongdoers will enjoy a clear conscience and receive rich blessings from God and the people. Upholding moral standards brings health and security to society.

Speaking a truthful, straightforward answer to a question is as deeply appreciated as a friendly kiss on the lips. When someone gives honest, clear counsel without flattery or deceit, it wins the respect and gratitude of the hearer. Sincere words build trust and strengthen relationships.

Good planning means preparing fields and securing a steady livelihood before spending time and money to build or furnish a house. A person needs to establish the work that produces income first, rather than rushing into domestic expenses or comforts they cannot afford. Wise order in daily labor protects a family from financial ruin.

A person must never volunteer damaging testimony against a neighbor without a just and necessary reason. Speaking half-truths or using misleading words to ruin someone's reputation is a form of deceit. God calls his people to guard the good name of others rather than spreading unnecessary accusations.

Scripture forbids seeking personal revenge by paying back an offender with the same harm he caused. Taking justice into our own hands violates God's law of love and robs the Lord of his rightful place as the righteous judge. Believers are commanded to leave repayment to God rather than settling personal scores.

Solomon describes walking past the farm of an idle, foolish man and seeing complete decay. Weeds and thorns had taken over the productive soil, and the stone protective wall had crumbled away. Laziness inevitably ruins valuable gifts and leaves a person's life exposed to damage.

The teacher paused, looked carefully at the neglected farm, and took a vital lesson to heart. Wise people learn valuable truths not only from good examples, but also by observing the mistakes and failures of foolish people. Reflecting on the painful results of bad choices helps us grow in understanding.

The lazy owner constantly begs for just a little more sleep, a little more rest, and a quick nap. Because of these repeated excuses, sudden poverty marches toward him like a traveling robber, and deep want overpowers him like an armed bandit. Small daily compromises with laziness quickly end in complete financial ruin.
